title: AML Approval Endpoints at FDA and EMA: Complete Remission, Event-Free Survival and Overall Survival in Pivotal Trials
summary: How FDA and EMA weigh complete remission, event-free survival and overall survival as AML approval endpoints, with pivotal trial precedents.
body_markdown:
## AML approval endpoints at FDA and EMA: complete remission, event-free survival and overall survival in pivotal trials


Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) approvals rest on three main efficacy endpoint families: overall survival (OS), event-free survival (EFS), and remission-based endpoints (complete remission (CR), CR with partial hematologic recovery (CRh), and their composites). Which endpoint a regulator accepts depends mostly on the treatment intent (curative, noncurative or palliative), whether the product is added to intensive chemotherapy, and whether a randomized comparison is feasible. This article summarizes the current FDA and EMA framework and the pivotal trial precedents behind US and EU AML approvals, refusals and withdrawals.


### Key takeaways


- **FDA's 2022 final AML guidance links endpoints to treatment intent.** For curative-intent therapy, OS, EFS and relapse-free survival (RFS) support traditional approval, and FDA expects a randomized control arm rather than historical controls[501](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=501)[502](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=502) . For noncurative therapy, OS, EFS and durable CR are acceptable, and single-arm trials may be possible[503](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=503) . For palliative-intent therapy, durable CR and durable CR/CRh with transfusion independence are acceptable clinical-benefit endpoints[504](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=504) .
- **EMA takes a more conservative line on remission endpoints.** The CHMP anticancer guideline accepts CR as a primary endpoint mainly where later consolidation or maintenance could confound EFS, and it expects CR results to be supported by EFS or PFS data[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=68) . Superiority on EFS, PFS or OS is generally expected when toxicity increases[77](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=77) .
- **Randomized, OS-driven trials dominate newly diagnosed and maintenance approvals in both regions.** Examples are midostaurin (RATIFY), quizartinib (QuANTUM-First), CPX-351, glasdegib and venetoclax (VIALE-A), plus oral azacitidine (QUAZAR) in the maintenance setting[145](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=145)[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=174)[176](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=176)[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=151)[603](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=603)[123](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=123) .
- **EFS has supported approval in both jurisdictions,** for gemtuzumab ozogamicin (ALFA-0701) and ivosidenib plus azacitidine (AGILE)[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=159)[205](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=205)[241](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=241)[395](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=395) .
- **Single-arm CR/CRh trials diverge sharply between the agencies.** In relapsed/refractory (R/R), molecularly targeted settings, FDA granted regular approval on single-arm CR/CRh data to enasidenib, ivosidenib, olutasidenib and ziftomenib[704](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=704)[674](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=674)[627](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=627)[645](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=645) . Gilteritinib's November 2018 regular approval used an interim CR/CRh rate from the randomized ADMIRAL trial[636](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=636) . EMA refused a single-arm, CR-based gemtuzumab ozogamicin application, and the single-arm ivosidenib R/R application was withdrawn[246](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=246)[27](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=27) .


### The regulatory framework


#### FDA: Acute Myeloid Leukemia guidance (final, October 2022)


FDA's *Acute Myeloid Leukemia: Developing Drugs and Biological Products for Treatment* was finalized on October 17, 2022[548](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=548) . It sets out the following endpoint definitions:


- **CR:** marrow blasts <5% by morphology, ANC >1 Gi/L, platelets >100 Gi/L, no peripheral blood leukemic blasts, and no extramedullary disease[567](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=567) . The CR date is the marrow sampling date, and the protocol should set a maximum window between marrow and blood tests (3 to 7 days may be justifiable)[568](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=568) . Missing data count as failure to achieve CR[569](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=569) .
- **CRh:** the same marrow, peripheral blast and extramedullary criteria, but with ANC >0.5 Gi/L and platelets >50 Gi/L, without meeting CR count-recovery criteria[570](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=570)[571](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=571) . CRh applies to relatively nontoxic, nonmyelosuppressive drugs that may be used for palliation. In that setting the endpoint is CR+CRh, with follow-up long enough to establish meaningful durability[574](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=574)[575](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=575) .
- **Duration of CR:** time from CR to hematological relapse or death from any cause, with enough follow-up to show the remission is meaningfully durable[573](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=573) .
- **Transfusion independence (TI):** applicable to relatively nontoxic, nonmyelosuppressive drugs and should be supported by evidence of antileukemic activity[15](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=15) . FDA asks for prespecified transfusion rules, separate analyses for patients who were transfusion-dependent and transfusion-independent at baseline, and separate red cell and platelet TI analyses[16](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=16) .
- **OS and EFS:** OS is measured from randomization to death from any cause[9](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=9) . EFS counts induction treatment failure, relapse after induction success, or death, whichever occurs first[10](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=10)[11](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=11) .


For binary endpoints, the analysis set is all treated patients in single-arm trials and all randomized patients in randomized trials, with proportions reported with 95% confidence intervals[17](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=17) . For add-on designs, a placebo comparator can be considered when the control arm receives appropriate treatment (for example, study drug plus 7+3 versus placebo plus 7+3)[505](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=505) . Best supportive care is a possible randomized comparator in the palliative setting only when patients have no available therapies. A single-arm trial may be appropriate when adequate historical data support the null hypothesis[504](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=504) .


FDA's separate guidance on minimal residual disease (MRD) in hematologic malignancies describes MRD as a potential response measure, prognostic tool or trial-allocation biomarker[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=6) . It does not set out a standalone AML MRD efficacy endpoint.


FDA review documents add context on how the agency weighs these endpoints. The Division describes EFS and OS as direct measures of clinical benefit that have been used for regular approval[268](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=268)[277](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=277) . It describes durable CR as reasonably likely to predict long-term benefit[268](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=268)[269](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=269) . In the noncurative, palliative setting, it states that durable CR+CRh has been used for regular approval of nonmyelosuppressive, reasonably nontoxic drugs[271](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=271)[268](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=268) . TI is treated as corroborating evidence. In the quizartinib R/R review, FDA stated that TI alone could not establish benefit[276](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=276) .


#### EMA: anticancer guideline and the haematological malignancies appendix


EMA has no AML-specific guideline. The relevant recommendations are in the CHMP *Guideline on the evaluation of anticancer medicinal products in man* , under the section on treatment administered with curative intent[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=70)[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=71)[72](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=72)[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=73) . Revision 6 repeats the EFS definition. It also notes that treatment complexity in AML can make it hard to show an effect on cure rate or survival[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=67) .


- **EFS:** events are failure to achieve CR during the prespecified induction phase (assigned an event at time zero), relapse, and death without relapse. Analysis of a primary EFS endpoint should wait until the data are sufficiently mature[74](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=74)[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=75) .
- **CR as primary endpoint:** acceptable when reduced or similar toxicity is expected and consolidation or maintenance could confound EFS/PFS. CR should be supported by EFS or PFS data and assessed with established criteria. A CR plus partial response composite needs specific justification[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=68) .
- **Design by toxicity profile:**


- Reduced or similar toxicity: substitution non-inferiority designs are acceptable, usually with an EFS or PFS primary endpoint[76](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=76) .
- Increased toxicity: superiority in EFS, PFS or OS is generally expected. A major increase in post-induction CR with favourable time-to-event trends may suffice in small populations[77](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=77) .
- Major increase in toxicity: increased cure rate or improved OS is expected[78](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=78) .


- **MRD:** molecular MRD is supportive evidence for CR and should be used only after intra- and inter-laboratory validation[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=71)[79](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=79) . The draft haematological malignancies appendix treats MRD-defined response as supportive evidence in very small target populations. It also calls for justified eligibility criteria, response criteria and reference therapy in confirmatory studies[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=80)[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=69) .


### Overall survival as the primary endpoint


OS is the most common primary endpoint in randomized AML registration trials at both agencies.


Product (trial) Setting and design Primary endpoint and result FDA / EMA notes


Midostaurin (RATIFY / Study A2301) Newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML, ages 18 to 59. Randomized, double-blind; midostaurin vs placebo added to induction and consolidation chemotherapy, then maintenance (n=717)[223](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=223)[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=224) OS, HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.63 to 0.95)[145](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=145) EMA: OS without censoring at transplant; HR 0.774, median 74.74 vs 25.59 months[225](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=225)[226](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=226)[227](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=227) . The maintenance phase was neither separately randomized nor powered[61](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=61)


Quizartinib (QuANTUM-First) Newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD-positive AML. Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled add-on to chemotherapy, then maintenance (n=539)[172](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=172)[173](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=173) OS, HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.62 to 0.98)[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=174) CHMP considered the OS benefit established with reasonable certainty despite weak statistical strength. The key secondary EFS analysis was not significant[420](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=420)[421](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=421)[422](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=422)


CPX-351 (Vyxeos, Study 301) Ages 60 to 75 with high-risk/secondary AML. Randomized, open-label vs 7+3 (n=309)[289](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=289)[290](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=290) OS, median 9.6 vs 5.9 months, HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.52 to 0.90)[176](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=176)[177](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=177)[291](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=291)[292](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=292) CR and CR+CRi were secondary endpoints at EMA (37% vs 26%; 48% vs 33%)[293](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=293)[294](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=294)


Glasdegib + LDAC (BRIGHT AML 1003 / B1371003) Newly diagnosed AML, unfit for intensive induction. Randomized 2:1, open-label vs LDAC alone[436](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=436)[437](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=437)[438](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=438) OS, median 8.3 vs 4.3 months, HR 0.46[151](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=151)[152](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=152)[441](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=441) FDA: regular approval[679](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=679) . CHMP accepted the design, LDAC as comparator, and OS and CR as endpoints[443](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=443)


Venetoclax + azacitidine (VIALE-A / M15-656) Untreated AML, ineligible for intensive chemotherapy. Randomized, placebo-controlled (n=431)[599](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=599)[518](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=518) OS, median 14.7 vs 9.6 months, HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.52 to 0.85)[603](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=603)[519](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=519) EMA: OS and CR+CRi were co-primary endpoints; CR+CRi 65.3% vs 25.3% at the interim analysis[518](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=518)[520](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=520)


Oral azacitidine (QUAZAR / CC-486-AML-001) Maintenance in first CR/CRi. Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled[485](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=485)[122](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=122) OS, median 24.7 vs 14.8 months, HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.55 to 0.86)[123](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=123)[124](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=124) CHMP noted weaker evidence of benefit in the CRi and MRD-negative subgroups[488](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=488)


Gilteritinib (ADMIRAL / 2215-CL-0301) R/R FLT3-mutated AML. Randomized 2:1, open-label vs salvage chemotherapy (n=371)[311](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=311)[312](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=312)[313](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=313) Final OS, median 9.3 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.49 to 0.83)[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=133)[134](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=134)[317](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=317)[318](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=318) EMA: OS and CR/CRh were co-primary, but CHMP treated final OS as the primary efficacy measure[314](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=314)[316](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=316)


Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (AML-19) Older or unfit newly diagnosed AML. Randomized, open-label vs best supportive care[162](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=162) OS, median 4.9 vs 3.6 months, HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.53 to 0.90)[163](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=163) FDA label


#### OS trials that missed statistical significance


EMA precedents show that CHMP has accepted clinically meaningful OS gains even when the primary test was not formally met.


- **Decitabine (Dacogen), DACO-016.** This open-label phase 3 trial compared decitabine with patient's choice of supportive care or low-dose cytarabine. The primary OS analysis gave HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.69 to 1.04; p=0.1079), which was not statistically significant. With an additional year of follow-up, the HR was 0.82 (nominal p=0.0373)[329](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=329)[330](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=330)[332](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=332)[333](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=333)[334](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=334) . CHMP considered the 2.7-month median survival gain clinically meaningful in this setting, while noting that significance was reached only in a second post hoc analysis[335](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=335) .
- **Azacitidine (Vidaza), AZA-AML-001.** In patients aged 65 or older with >30% marrow blasts, the OS comparison (median 10.4 vs 6.5 months, HR 0.85) did not reach its predefined significance level (p=0.1009). CHMP considered the endpoints, design and population appropriate[360](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=360)[361](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=361)[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=362)[363](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=363)[364](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=364) .
- **Venetoclax + LDAC (VIALE-C / M16-043).** The primary OS analysis did not meet its objective (HR 0.749; p=0.114). Higher CR and CR+CRi rates were therefore descriptive only[524](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=524)[525](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=525)[526](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=526) . An EMA expert group found the observed antitumor activity insufficient to formally establish an OS difference[511](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=511) .


### Event-free survival as the primary endpoint


**Gemtuzumab ozogamicin, ALFA-0701.** Both agencies accepted EFS from this randomized, open-label phase 3 trial. It added gemtuzumab ozogamicin to daunorubicin/cytarabine in 271 patients aged 50 to 70 with newly diagnosed de novo AML[158](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=158)[238](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=238)[239](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=239) . Median EFS was 17.3 vs 9.5 months (HR 0.56)[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=159)[241](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=241)[242](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=242) . CHMP considered EFS clinically meaningful. It noted that the benefit came from longer remissions, not more CRs, that the OS effect was less clear, and that efficacy in younger patients was extrapolated[243](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=243)[244](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=244) . In the pediatric AAML0531 study, FDA labeling describes EFS (HR 0.84) as supportive evidence[161](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=161) .


**Ivosidenib + azacitidine, AGILE (AG120-C-009).** This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial enrolled 146 adults with untreated IDH1-mutated AML who were ineligible for intensive induction[393](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=393)[394](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=394) . EFS was defined with treatment failure as failure to achieve CR by week 24. Median EFS was 22.9 vs 4.1 months (HR 0.39), and median OS was 24.0 vs 7.9 months (HR 0.44)[395](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=395)[396](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=396)[397](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=397) . FDA labeling reports the EFS HR as 0.35 (95% CI 0.17 to 0.72), from an analysis with a different cutoff[206](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=206)[400](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=400)[401](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=401) . CHMP raised design concerns that sponsors should note:


- the primary endpoint was changed from OS to EFS during the trial;
- the planned sample size was reduced;
- the trial was stopped early, in an unplanned way, using unblinded efficacy data.


CHMP concluded that type I error could not be formally controlled. It nevertheless acknowledged strong results supported by sensitivity analyses[398](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=398)[399](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=399) .


Leukemia-free survival has also served as a primary endpoint in remission-maintenance settings, for example in the EU assessment of histamine dihydrochloride with interleukin-2 (Ceplene)[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=41)[43](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=43) .


### CR and CR+CRh as the approval endpoint


#### FDA: regular approval on durable remission


In R/R AML with a defined molecular target, FDA has repeatedly granted **regular approval** on durable CR or CR/CRh. Most of these approvals rested on single-arm trials; gilteritinib's used an interim CR/CRh analysis from the randomized ADMIRAL trial. Rate and duration were the efficacy basis. Transfusion independence was supportive when shown, and was not required for revumenib[275](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=275) .


Product (trial) Population Remission result Approval type

Ivosidenib monotherapy in newly diagnosed patients was also labeled on a single-arm CR+CRh rate (12/28, 42.9%)[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=209)[210](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=210)[211](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=211) .


#### EMA: single-arm remission data are scrutinized more closely


EU outcomes for single-arm CR-based applications have been less favorable:


- **Gemtuzumab ozogamicin, first-relapse application (refused).** The application rested on three single-arm trials with a CR primary endpoint (CR 13%, plus 13% CRp)[245](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=245) . CHMP judged the CR rate modest and reliable data on valid clinical endpoints lacking. It stated that a full application should have relied on randomized controlled trials[246](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=246) .
- **Ivosidenib, R/R application (withdrawn).** The pivotal study was single-arm with a CR+CRh primary endpoint[384](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=384)[388](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=388) . CHMP advice had stressed the need for a patient-level matched historical control. CHMP later questioned whether an OS difference against such a control (HR 0.396) was caused by treatment, given likely residual confounding. It also noted that response-based OS comparisons suffer from immortal-time bias[389](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=389)[390](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=390)[391](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=391) .
- **CPX-351, pediatric relapsed AML (accepted).** CHMP accepted the single uncontrolled AAML1421 study, with a CR+CRp primary endpoint (68% response), as adequate for the pediatric relapsed indication. It acknowledged the limitation of a single uncontrolled study[296](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=296)[297](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=297)[298](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=298)[299](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=299) .


### Accelerated approval and confirmatory trials at FDA


Two FDA precedents show how accelerated approval has been used in AML:


- **Venetoclax.** The AML indication received accelerated approval on November 21, 2018. FDA required the final report from phase 3 trial M16-043 (venetoclax plus LDAC vs LDAC), with OS as the primary endpoint[477](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=477)[478](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=478) . Traditional approval followed on October 16, 2020, primarily on confirmatory OS from VIALE-A. VIALE-C was also reviewed but had not met its primary OS endpoint[479](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=479)[480](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=480) .
- **Gemtuzumab ozogamicin.** Accelerated approval was granted on May 17, 2000, in first-relapse AML. The required confirmatory trial (SWOG S0106) failed to verify clinical benefit, and the product was withdrawn in 2010. It returned with regular approval on September 1, 2017, based on new data in newly diagnosed and R/R AML[660](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=660)[661](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=661)[662](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=662) .


### Negative and borderline precedents


- **Quizartinib, R/R FLT3-ITD AML (refused by EMA).** AC220-007 was an open-label, randomized OS trial against salvage chemotherapy[423](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=423)[424](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=424) . CHMP called the primary OS result borderline positive. It found efficacy not established because missing data and non-administrative censoring, mostly in the open-label control arm, undermined the result. EFS and CR did not support the OS finding[425](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=425)[426](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=426) .
- **Vosaroxin (Qinprezo, withdrawn).** The EU application was based on an adaptive-design, placebo-comparator R/R AML study with an OS primary endpoint[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=56)[58](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=58) .


### FDA and EMA at a glance


Dimension FDA EMA


Curative-intent / intensive settings OS, EFS or RFS for traditional approval, with a randomized control arm required[501](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=501)[502](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=502) Superiority on EFS, PFS or OS when toxicity increases. Non-inferiority, usually on EFS or PFS, when toxicity is similar or lower[76](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=76)[77](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=77)


CR as a basis for approval Durable CR acceptable in noncurative settings; durable CR/CRh with TI in palliative settings[503](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=503)[504](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=504) Primary CR acceptable mainly where post-induction therapy confounds EFS, and should be supported by EFS/PFS[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=68)


Single-arm trials Acceptable in noncurative and palliative settings. Several R/R regular approvals rest on CR/CRh[503](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=503)[504](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=504)[674](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=674)[627](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=627) Refused or withdrawn applications show an expectation of randomized evidence or a well-matched control[246](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=246)[389](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=389)[390](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=390)


MRD Discussed as a response measure, prognostic tool or biomarker[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=6) Supportive evidence for CR after assay validation[71](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=71)[79](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=79)


Co-primary endpoints OS is the label efficacy basis in VIALE-A and ADMIRAL[603](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=603)[133](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=133) VIALE-A (OS + CR+CRi) and ADMIRAL (OS + CR/CRh) were assessed as co-primary[518](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=518)[314](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=314)


### Practical implications for AML development programs


- **Frontline intensive or add-on programs** should plan a randomized trial with an OS or EFS primary endpoint. Placebo-controlled add-on designs on standard chemotherapy are accepted by both agencies, as RATIFY and QuANTUM-First show[501](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=501)[505](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=505)[145](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=145)[174](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=174)[224](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=224)[414](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=414) .
- **Protocol integrity matters at EMA.** Changing the primary endpoint mid-trial, reducing the sample size, or stopping early on unblinded data can undermine an otherwise strong EFS result[398](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=398)[399](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=399) . Heavy censoring in an open-label control arm can undermine an OS result[426](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=426) .
- **Single-arm CR/CRh programs in biomarker-defined R/R populations** have a well-established FDA regular-approval pathway. Sponsors still need to show durability and supportive TI data, and FDA adjudication of response can lower the observed rate relative to the prespecified benchmark[271](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=271)[545](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=545) . In the EU, sponsors should expect to justify single-arm evidence with a patient-level external control and to address confounding and immortal-time bias[389](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=389)[390](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=390)[391](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=391) .
- **Remission data alone rarely carry an EU application.** CHMP repeatedly asks whether CR translates into EFS or OS, and has framed CR, CRi and MRD as supportive rather than decisive[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=68)[243](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=243)[420](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=420)[488](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/aml-approval-endpoints-at-fda-and-ema-complete?showSourceNumber=488) .
